/LILIAN

Baltic Exchange Market Report 29 October 2026
Baltic Dry Index: 2712 (60)
Baltic Capesize Index: 4090 (204)
Baltic Panamax Index: 1921 (-44)
Baltic Supramax Index: 1870 (-8)
Baltic Handysize Index: 1015 (-2)
CAPESIZE
The positive momentum carried through into Thursday, with both basins continuing to strengthen and the BCI 182 5TC rising by $1,850 to settle at $37,095. The C5 index gained a further $0.605 to $15.105, while C3 advanced by $0.980 to $36.485, reflecting improving sentiment across the board. In the Pacific, two C5 miners were in the market, with offers opening in the mid-$15s. A degree of resistance emerged during the afternoon as buyers and sellers briefly stood their ground, before one miner was reported to have paid in the low $15s. Despite the temporary standoff, the underlying tone remained firm, with owners continuing to push for higher levels. Atlantic conditions also strengthened, following a particularly active day yesterday for South Brazil and West Africa to China. Brokers reported that at least 8–10 fixtures had been concluded, tightening the ballaster list and providing further support to rates. The latest confirmed C3 business from yesterday included $36.00 for an ETA of 20/21 November and $36.60 for 1/7 December. Rumours circulated today of a further fixture at $36.68, although this remained unconfirmed. With both basins maintaining their upward trajectory, the market closed on a firm note. Continued Atlantic activity and a tightening supply of ballasters, alongside resilient Pacific demand, have helped sustain the recovery, with attention now turning to whether this momentum can carry into the end of the week.
PANAMAX
The Atlantic market continued to reflect the negative sentiment seen throughout the week, with fundamentals remaining imbalanced. Trans-Atlantic demand is said to remain thin, while the limited bids in the market continue to push lower and the North Continent remains under pressure. Some brokers suggested that owners with the flexibility to wait until next week may choose to do so, hoping for a fresh injection of cargo to help arrest the decline in rates. Fronthaul conditions from EC South America are showing some signs of improvement, with demand picking up despite the continued influx of ballasting tonnage from the Indian Ocean. Market participants have highlighted pockets of positivity, providing owners with some renewed optimism and encouraging them to hold firmer on their rate ideas. The Girasole River (81,982 2020) open Hazira 18/20 October fixed a trip via EC South America to Singapore-Japan range at $20,000 to Cargill, while the Theordore JR (81,715 2015) Krishnapatnam 19/20 October fixed a similar trip at around $20,250 plus $1,000,250 ballast bonus, but the charterer was unknown. The HC Glory (75,416 2012) open Tuna Tekra 20 Oct also fixed for a fronthaul with some suggesting the rate to be in the upper $18,000’s plus upper $800,000’s ballast bonus. Conditions across the Pacific weakened further today, with the softer tone in the Atlantic increasingly influencing sentiment in the East. Although the underlying supply and demand balance remained relatively stable, market sources stated that charterers appeared content to hold back as owners gradually revised their rate expectations. North Pacific grains continued to attract discounted levels compared with mineral business, while a noticeable reduction in EC Australian requirements added to the downward pressure. Indonesian activity offered some stability, although the possibility of further vessels repositioning from the Indian Ocean suggested that competition for available cargoes could intensify in the coming days. The P5TC declined today by $397 to $17,289.
SUPRAMAX
After yesterday’s holiday in Greece the market was more active today, although apart from the Far East, routes were negative with the 11TC average down $92 to settle at $23,641. US Gulf rates continue to ease with insufficient fresh enquiry to soak up the committed tonnage, whilst the south Atlantic has also come under pressure despite a tighter tonnage list, as the Panamax market competes on certain stems. In Asia rates are holding in light trading, which it turn held period rates up. A Dolphin 64,000-dwt open EC India was fixed for 3 to 5 months at $23,500, but further details were elusive.

Atlantic
The Abilene (63,127 2017) prompt in US East coast went on subjects basis delivery Puerto Brisa for a trip to the Black Sea with coal redelivery Canakkale at $35,000 with Centurion and there was a rumour that Bunge recently fixed a Japanese built 61,000-dwt delivery Recalada for a trip South East Asia at $18,250 plus $825,000 ballast bonus.

Asia
Fullinks were said to have taken a Supramax open Indonesia for a trip China with coal at $18,000, the Norse Addition (66,252 2025) open Acajutla apparently agreed $30,000 for a trip via NoPac back to the Far East and the Famiglia (63,425 2023) open Manzanillo fixed a similar trip at $31,000, but there were no further details on any of these fixtures.
HANDYSIZE
There was only one negative route in the Index today, but the drop was enough to move the HS7TC average down $30 to $18,274, with a source suggesting US Gulf bids were now mid teens on a BHSI38. Changes elsewhere were minimal, with the market appearing balanced in other areas of the Atlantic and South East Asia, whilst the North Pacific edged up despite sources saying tonnage seemed plentiful. East coast South America looked flat today, after its recent hot streak, but rates are still very firm. The Amity (29,996 2012) Vitoria 27-29 October fixed basis delivery Recalada for a trip to the Far East with Axle Marine at $15,000 and the Saint Vassilios (33,889 2012) Fortaleza 7-12 November agreed a trip via Pecem to Bremen, apparently to cover at Arcelormittal stem, but the reported rate of $27,000 to Cosmotrade was said to be incorrect with the correct details yet to surface.

HRB Steel Prices

In the fortnight to 28 October, the US hot rolled band (HRB) price rose $47/t to more than a four-year high of $1,357/t, World Steel Dynamics data show. In contrast, the Chinese and Western Europe HRB price eased $4/t and $7/t to $418/t and $828/t, respectively.
